scenario: An `after` body lowers with its rule's types, as the rule's own body does. Rule `plan` arms a 1 s timer for a Visit on 2024-02-29 (day 19782); its follow-up logs `due {v.due}`, a bare Date interpolation ([LGRA.2.9.6.10]), and emits a Shifted with `next: v.due + 1_d` ([RLOW.6.1.5]'s FN_DATE_ADD_DURATION) and `text: (v.due - 7_d)::String` (FN_DATE_SUB_DURATION, then a cast that dispatches on its operand's static type). Rule `show` logs the Shifted. Messages: `due 2024-02-29`, `1 2024-03-01 2024-02-22`. The breaks: a follow-up lowered with no typing environment leaves the cast unlowered, so the rule is skipped and nothing is logged; were the cast removed, `v.due + 1_d` would be Int `+` on a day count and nanoseconds, a Date about 86 trillion days later, and `{v.due}` would render the day count `19782`. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete`'s `after` follow-up context (`ltac_3_1_afters`), whose `cx_env` carries the rule's `type_env`, read by `rlow_6_1_5_date_arith`, `cast_fn` and `lgra_2_9_6_10_temporal_text`.
rules_ds:
schema Visit scope logical:
    id: Int key
    due: Date mutable

schema Shifted scope ttl 1_h:
    id: Int
    next: Date
    text: String

rule plan:
    Visit v
->
    after 1_s:
        log info "due {v.due}"
        emit Shifted id: v.id next: v.due + 1_d text: (v.due - 7_d)::String

rule show:
    Shifted s
->
    log info "{s.id} {s.next} {s.text}"
